title: Banks sell-off ends four-week rally; Nifty slumps 1.75%, Rupee weakens - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Profit-booking in heavyweight banking stocks, weakness in metals and investor caution ahead of Tuesday’s market holiday amid geopolitical uncertainties triggered a sharp sell-off on Dalal Street on Monday, wiping out opening gains and snapping a four-week rally.

The Nifty 50 plunged 450.95 points, or 1.75 per cent, to close at 25,349.65, while the Sensex tumbled 1,483.72 points, or 1.77 per cent, to 82,435.99.

The sell-off was particularly severe as the benchmarks had opened sharply higher, buoyed by strong foreign inflows, before profit-booking on the November monthly F&O expiry day erased early gains.

From its intraday high of 25,992.60, just shy of the 26,000 mark, the Nifty lost nearly 650 points before settling near the day’s low, highlighting the intensity of the reversal.

Dinesh C Nagpal, a full-time trader and investor, said monthly expiry dynamics amplified volatility, with key open-interest levels triggering short-covering and stop-losses before the market eventually turned sharply lower.

“Monday’s fall reads as a positioning reset rather than the end of India’s November recovery,” said Hemant Sood, Founder and Managing Director of Findoc Group. He noted that both the Sensex and Nifty remain nearly 10 per cent higher for the month, supported by about $13 billion of foreign portfolio inflows.

The sharp correction was led by banking stocks, which had been among the strongest performers during the recent rally. The Bank Nifty slumped 3.17 per cent, or 2,049.85 points, to close at 62,585.35 after touching a record high of 65,193.40 earlier in the day. Axis Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank ended lower, while the PSU Bank index dropped more than 3 per cent.

“Banking stocks witnessed notable selling after their strong outperformance over the preceding four weeks, while metal stocks were weighed down by softer global commodity prices and a stronger US dollar,” said Ajit Mishra, SVP-Research, Religare Broking.

Market participants said caution ahead of Tuesday’s market holiday and concerns over geopolitical developments prompted investors to reduce risk exposure, particularly in banking and metal counters.

Metal stocks were another major drag, with the Nifty Metal index falling 3.68 per cent. Tata Steel plunged 8.4 per cent after announcing an agreement to transfer its tubes and colour-coated steel businesses to APL Apollo Tubes in a deal valued at up to ₹28,000 crore.

Global cues added to the pressure. The Nasdaq had fallen more than 5 per cent on Friday, while South Korea’s KOSPI declined 3.3 per cent on Monday, raising concerns over stretched valuations in AI-linked stocks and debt-funded data-centre investments.

“The domestic market remains vulnerable to profit booking after the recent sharp rally,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, adding that weakness in global equities could spill over into India, though the impact may be limited by the country’s resilient domestic economy.

The rupee also reversed course, snapping a four-session winning streak. After opening stronger at ₹92.5 against the dollar and appreciating to ₹92.4, the currency weakened sharply through the day to close 23 paise lower at ₹92.9.

Dealers attributed the reversal to profit-booking after the recent appreciation, importer demand and dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India to meet requirements under the oil-marketing company window.

Traders said the rupee’s decline mirrored the broader risk-off sentiment in equities, even as lower crude oil prices and continued foreign inflows offered some support to the domestic currency.

“After this continuous rally, the market also deserves some retracement,” said V.R.C. Reddy, Head of Treasury at Karur Vysya Bank, adding that the market was witnessing a natural pullback after a sustained rise.

Market breadth remained weak, with 2,274 stocks declining against 1,028 advances on the NSE. The Nifty Midcap 100 fell 1.01 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 declined 0.66 per cent, indicating that selling extended beyond index heavyweights. India VIX rose 2.18 per cent to 17.7, signalling heightened caution among investors.
